parts.subtitle: Izon is a New Zealand company specialising in nanoscience – the study of atoms, molecules and other very small pieces of matter.
parts.article:
Think Small
 
Izon is a New Zealand company specialising in nanoscience – the study of atoms, molecules and other very small pieces of matter.
 
(A) The new US headquarters of Izon are situated in Cambridge, Massachusetts, one of the most important global centres of scientific research and technology. Half the other offices in the building Izon shares have scientific names like Stemgent, or the word 'pharmaceutical' in the name. In the past three years, Izon has expanded to 17 times its previous size. It's done so selling only one product that it's been developing since 2004, the qNano. This is an adjustable tool for the measurement and analysis of tiny particles in scientific research, which comes with a $27,000 price tag. Izon's success results from the fact that the qNano machine provides precise measurements, while similar machines of the same price only offer averaging techniques. In effect, researchers using the qNano are able to gather information about very small things, and it has many possible applications from drug delivery analysis through to environmental research.
 
(B) Kristoffer Bolen is Izon's US head of sales. Alongside his full-time role with the company, he's just finished the fifth semester of six for his High-Tech Master of Business Administration at Northeastern University, which will be his second master's degree, alongside a Master of Science. These soon-to-be twin master's degrees provide Bolen with the perfect combination of skills for his job, which depends on him being able to manage the sales process and also comprehend in depth a very complicated piece of technology. When a customer buys a qNano device, an Izon representative will fly anywhere in America to train them how to use the instrument. The representative then checks in with the client on an ongoing basis to be completely informed about how each qNano is being used, and then liaises with technicians back in New Zealand.
 
(C) The Izon story started 8 years ago in New Zealand. Hans van der Voorn was aimless, having sold his own company, and was looking for something more taxing to set his mind to. Van der Voorn was introduced to three scientists with an idea that involved simply a small plastic membrane with a tiny adjustable hole to measure a range of very small particles. Initially he put up an investment of $1.5 million to move the process forward to the development of a prototype, and this led to the founding of Izon and the production of the qNano. Van der Voorn believes that the worlds of science and business sometimes don't understand each other very well. However, he thinks that engineering can be a bridge between the two, and his long experience in that field has been crucial to the company's success. He soon realised that Izon was going to need people on the ground overseas if it was going to grow, so the US office was opened. For now Izon trades in the US as a foreign company, so avoids the high level of compliance that comes with being an American-registered company. But he sees that one day soon this will change, as Izon's current position disallows it from entering into partnerships locally.
 
(D) Marketing the qNano is complicated. Izon needs scientists both to buy and advertise the product. The science world may seem like a big playing field, but it's actually a small group. As a result, the critical part of the company's marketing is articles that clients publish describing work they have performed with the qNano. So for Izon the sale isn't enough in itself; it also has a stake in how customers are using the qNano. That's where Yaniv Gaynor comes in. As development and training manager, he's involved throughout the sales process and manages most of the customer's post-sale experience. The sales process is new for Gaynor, who shifted cities and switched from a role as teacher at the University of Minnesota to his first private sector role with Izon. 'It's tricky, it's challenging, and it's not in my comfort zone,' he concedes. But nine out of ten times, if there's an unhappy customer, he's able to turn their experience around. And there's another part to this, because sitting with customers as they learn about the qNano, Gaynor gets to see how they are using the product. 'People ask very good questions, and these are great triggers for future development,' he says.
 
(E) 'Our business is selling research tools,' van der Voorn says. But he knows that the application range of this tool is wide. For instance, Izon is engaged in a project with Harvard University, looking for a particular type of particle of blood that is a symptom of the medical condition of thrombosis. If in the future they can identify this particle, they can design a simple test for it. This would make it easier for doctors to diagnose thrombosis. Another planned development is eventually to shift the US base to more spacious offices on the other side of town. With larger headquarters, the company will be able to bring clients into the Izon building for training with its product, rather than travelling to them, which will hopefully result in an even closer relationship between the company and its customers.

questions.question: Izon's new US headquarters are located in an area popular with other science businesses.

analyses.content: 不要只找“popular”这个词，文中用周围邻居都是同行（Half the other offices...）来侧面印证这一点的。
(A) Half the other offices in the building Izon shares have scientific names like Stemgent, or the word 'pharmaceutical' in the name.
文章A段提到，Izon所在的办公楼里，有一半的其他办公室都带有“scientific names（科学名称）”或“pharmaceutical（制药）”字样，说明这里确实是科学企业的聚集地。

questions.question: Izon's growth in the last three years has been faster than the company predicted.

analyses.content: 文章A段虽然提到了公司规模扩大了“17 times（17倍）”，但这只是一个客观事实，并没有提及公司之前是否“predicted（预测）”了增长速度，也没有说实际速度是否比预测的快。
不要看到“17倍”就觉得很快、进而觉得超出了预期，文中没提“预期”就是没提。
(A) In the past three years, Izon has expanded to 17 times its previous size.

questions.question: Since 2004, Izon has developed a range of equipment for use in scientific research.

analyses.content: 文章A段明确指出，Izon至今只销售“only one product（唯一一种产品）”，即qNano，这与题目中的“a range of equipment（一系列/多种设备）”直接矛盾。
看到“only one”就能直接否定“range of”，不要因为后面提到该产品有多种“applications（应用）”就混淆了产品本身的单一性。
(A) It's done so selling only one product that it's been developing since 2004, the qNano.

questions.question: One advantage of the qNano is that it is cheaper than its competitors.

analyses.content: 看到“same price”就知道“cheaper”是错的，不要看到价格数字（$27,000）就自己主观判断贵贱。
文章A段进行对比时说，类似机器是“of the same price（同样价格）”，qNano的优势在于提供精确测量而非平均值，并不是因为更便宜。
(A) Izon's success results from the fact that the qNano machine provides precise measurements, while similar machines of the same price only offer averaging techniques.

questions.question: Drug delivery analysis will be the most profitable application of the qNano.

analyses.content: 文章A段末尾确实提到了“drug delivery analysis（药物输送分析）”作为应用之一，但完全没有提及它是否是“most profitable（最赚钱的）”。
文中只是列举了应用范围（from... to...），并没有对这些应用的盈利能力进行排名。
(A) ...and it has many possible applications from drug delivery analysis through to environmental research.

questions.question: Kristoffer Bolen is still completing his studies.

analyses.content: 文章B段提到Bolen刚完成了六个学期中的“fifth semester（第五个学期）”，说明他还没毕业，确实还在“completing his studies（完成学业中）”。
看到“finished”别急着选False，看清楚是finished semester（完成学期）而不是finished degree（完成学位）。
(B) ...he's just finished the fifth semester of six for his High-Tech Master of Business Administration...

questions.question: Bolen's job requires him to fully understand how the qNano works.

analyses.content: (B) ...skills for his job, which depends on him being able to manage the sales process and also comprehend in depth a very complicated piece of technology.
词汇替换题，“comprehend in depth”就是“fully understand”的高级表达。
文章B段说他的工作依赖于能够“comprehend in depth（深入理解）”这台复杂的设备，这与“fully understand”意思一致。

analyses.content: 定位到C段，Hans van der Voorn提供了150万美元的“investment（投资）”来推动原型机的开发。
题目中的“made the...”对应文中的动词短语“put up an...”，核心名词是investment。
(C) Initially he put up an investment of $1.5 million to move the process forward to the development of a prototype...
定位到C段，文中说他认为“engineering（工程学）”是科学与商业的桥梁，他在该领域的经验至关重要。
题目结构是“... as well as business”，文中对应的是“bridge between the two”（科学与商业），具体指代��文提到的engineering。
(C) However, he thinks that engineering can be a bridge between the two, and his long experience in that field has been crucial to the company's success.
(D) As a result, the critical part of the company's marketing is articles that clients publish describing work they have performed with the qNano.
定位到D段关于Marketing的部分，文中说营销的关键部分是客户发表的描述其工作的“articles（文章/论文）”。
题目中的“relies on（依赖）”对应文中的“critical part... is...”，需要填具体的内容载体“articles”。
定位到D段介绍Yaniv Gaynor背景的地方，文中说他转行前在明尼苏达大学当“teacher（老师）”。
题目问的是“formerly（以前是）”，对应文中的“switched from a role as...”。
(D) ...who shifted cities and switched from a role as teacher at the University of Minnesota to his first private sector role with Izon.
定位到E段关于未来的计划，文中说如果能识别相关粒子，就可以设计一种简单的“test（测试）”来诊断血栓。
题目中的“developed”对应文中的“design”，填空处需要填名词。
(E) If in the future they can identify this particle, they can design a simple test for it.
文章E段最后提到，有了更大的总部，公司就可以把客户请到Izon大楼里来进行“training（培训）”，而不是员工出差去客户那里。
题目问什么事情将在总部完成（be done at...），对应文中“bring clients into the Izon building for...”。
(E) With larger headquarters, the company will be able to bring clients into the Izon building for training with its product, rather than travelling to them...
